newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT - Bankers Trust turnaround.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT - Bankers Trust turnaround.

text.p: A new management team at Bankers Trust New York Corp is starting to convince Wall Street that the company has started a turnaround and earnings are poised to grow rapidly.
The company has also been moving rapidly to beef up its staff in key areas such as risk management and high yield, adding about 25 new people in key positions over the past two months.
Among the new blood at Bankers Trust is David Marshall, who joined from Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce. At Bankers Trust, Marshall will be responsible for the technology infrastructure.

Another newcomer is Karen Horn, a former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland. Horn, who will head international private banking, came to Bankers Trust from Banc One Corp, where she headed the company's Cleveland banking unit.

In the risk management area, Bankers Trust has hired Kevin Ferrell, formerly a top executive and chief financial officer of McKesson Corp. Ferrell will be head of the risk management advisory business, one of the areas Wall Street analysts are counting on to be a main driver of a rebound in earnings.

Ochestrating the refocusing at Bankers Trust is Frank Newman, who came to the firm late last year from the U.S. Treassury, where he was deputy secretary. As of April, he holds the titles of chairman, chief executive and president.
With Bankers Trust's embarassing legal wrangling with long- time clients over soured derivatives deals now fading into history, some Wall Street analysts are taking a fresh look.
Goldman, Sachs & Co recently added Bankers Trust to the U.S. recommended list and set a share price target of $103 in 15 months, 26 percent higher than the current level.

However, many analysts remain on the fence. One of them, Raphael Soifer of Brown Brothers Harriman & Co, said the return on equity, currently 12 percent, pales alongside such companies as Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and Morgan Stanley Group Inc both of which have ROE's in the high 20's.
"I don't think 12 percent return on equity is acceptable for the business that Bankers Trust is in," Soifer said.

Robert Albertson, head of U.S. bank research at Goldman, Sachs, pointed to four factors that he considered positive for Bankers Trust. First, he said the company is an investment banking powerhouse in the high-yield sector, drawing on long experience. And a recent merger with Wolfensohn & Co brings relationships with a host of investment grade clients.
A second factor cited by Albertson is Bankers Trust's strong reputation and long history, with a solid customer base, in risk management.
Despite the past troubles with derivatives, Albertson said the market for risk management tools is growing.
Third, Albertson believes Bankers Trust's investment management business, with $176 billion under management, could be a big moneymaker in future years.
Finally, he said the stock of Bankers Trust is valued on an earnings or book value basis at the low end for commercial banks and at the high end for brokers.
But he said Bankers Trust is not a broker, as proprietary trading is less than 15 percent of earnings and the bulk of underwriting is not equties and therefore not dependent on a strong stock market.
Albertson estimates earnings at Bankers Trust will be $6.90 per share this year, rise 20 percent to $8.30 per share in 1997 and rise a further 24 percent to $10.30 in 1998.
Some risks in the rosy outlook, Albertson said, include the success and timing of the turnaround, market conditions and innate, although lessened, quarterly earnings volatility.
Lawrence Cohn of PaineWebber Group Inc, another of the analysts in the bullish camp, also sees potential for a "meaningful breakout in earnings" in derivatives.

And Leslie Nelkin, analyst at Furman Selz, cited the potential for earnings of $9.00 per share in 1997 and the support of the dividend. Despite turning more cautious on the balance of 1996, the analyst reaffirmed a buy rating.
Bankers Trust acquired Wolfensohn for about $210 million in cash and stock, according to filings with the U.S. Securites and Exchange Commission (SEC).
The head of Wolfensohn, former Federal Reserve chairman Paul Volcker, joined the boards of both the Bankers Trust New York holding company and the Bankers Trust Co banking subsidiary last month.
